title: Gradient boosting model separates PEA from VF as initial rhythm in cardiac arrest
summary: Using demographics and clinical variables from 421 EMS-witnessed out-of-hospital arrests in the Portland area, an extreme gradient boosting model separated PEA from VF as the true initial rhythm, with an AUC of 0.68 (95% CI 0.61-0.76). External validation in 220 EMS-witnessed arrests from Ventura, CA gave an AUC of 0.72 (95% CI 0.59-0.84). Anemia, older age, increased weight and dyspnea as a warning symptom weighed toward PEA. Performance is modest and the feature associations are observational, not causal.
ai_technology: Extreme gradient boosting model on demographics and detailed clinical variables

evidence.tested: Internal cohort of 421 EMS-witnessed arrests and external validation in 220 EMS-witnessed arrests from Ventura, CA.
evidence.unknown: Whether the predictors have a causal role or help develop treatments; performance beyond modest discrimination; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Predicts the true initial rhythm (PEA versus VF) and ranks the clinical features that drive the prediction.
